subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was found dead with his heart torn out and blackened finger and lip stains.
source_quote: There is a particular comfort in a corpse. It does not lie. It does not run a counter-play. Everything it knows is written on it, and all I have to do is read.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between Janussi’s dinner and his death, during which his nose was broken and he was assaulted.
source_quote: Within the evening — Janussi had eaten dinner with his face intact and his teeth whole. Whatever happened, happened in the narrow window between that meal and his death.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Janussi's final act
fact: Janussi was writing in blue ink on 'The Discoveries' moments before his death, smudging his finger and lip with poisoned ink.
source_quote: The blue ink on 'The Discoveries' had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. 'The Golden Ass.' 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: blackened finger stain
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s left forefinger and lower lip is not ink — it is a poison unknown even to an ooze that has consumed the Underdark.
source_quote: That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*.

subject: Keeper's chamber safe
fact: The safe in the Keeper's chamber contained a king's ransom in gold, platinum, diamonds, and potions — but one sapphire and one spell parchment were missing, indicating targeted theft, not robbery.
source_quote: Still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched. 'In other words, score what they left them.'

subject: broken lead chain links
fact: Two broken lead links were found beneath the Keeper’s neck, indicating a locket or necklace had been forcibly removed after he was struck but before he died.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain.

subject: dart impacts on armchair
fact: Three circular impacts and holes in the armchair suggest a magical dart weapon was fired at the chair — not the Keeper — indicating an outburst of rage directed at an object, not a person.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. Daz's mind clicked again — material components, every pouch a spell — and he murmured, 'a little bit of this, a little bit of that,' pleased with himself. But one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.'

subject: Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore statue
fact: The three-foot marble statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over by shock upon discovering the body — not by sabotage, but by an accidental collision.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: chipped tooth
fact: Janussi’s front tooth was chipped from a fall face-first onto stone — a recent trauma occurring just before death, unrelated to the heart removal.
source_quote: A chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent. Not an old break worn smooth, but a fresh wound. He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: silver pedestal and ebony pipe
fact: A silver pedestal and finely carved ebony pipe with cherry tobacco were found near the desk — the tobacco likely used to mask the scent of poison.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco. Pretty, until Zalthir's instinct landed it — tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: sequence of death
fact: Janussi was assaulted (broken nose), returned to his desk to write, ingested poison via ink-stained finger, fell face-first (chipped tooth), and was then murdered (heart removed, body rolled) by a deliberate, unhurried killer.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: blue ink in 'The Discoveries'
fact: The latest writing in Janussi’s hand was in blue ink on 'The Discoveries', recorded after notes in 'The Golden Ass', indicating his final intellectual activity was spell research.
source_quote: The blue ink on 'The Discoveries' had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. 'The Golden Ass.' 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: loot selection
fact: The killer took only one sapphire and one spell parchment from the safe — leaving behind a small treasury — indicating the theft was targeted for a specific spell, not greed.
source_quote: Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom. 'I mean, well, that can eliminate some former adventurers,' I said. The greedy don't leave the gold. This was a man who needed exactly one thing.

subject: Keeper's chamber entry
fact: The safe’s door was open and undamaged — no forced entry — indicating the killer had either the combination or a key, or the safe was not locked.
source_quote: Zalthir checked the lock. Open, but undamaged. No forced entry. The killer had the combination, or had no need of one.

subject: nose bruising
fact: The bruising around Janussi’s broken nose formed before death, as corpses cannot bruise — proving he was assaulted and injured hours before being killed.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed. My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died. Not the fall. Earlier.

subject: statue fall
fact: The statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore was knocked over accidentally by shock upon discovering the body — not by magic or sabotage.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.
